sermon.title: Three Revelations Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Three Revelations Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer introduces the book of Revelation through its opening verse, saying it gives three revelations: the revelation of Jesus Christ, the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and the revelation of the church. He teaches that Revelation is written to all of God’s servants, uses Romans 2 and Revelation 20 to show judgment by works and the Book of Life, and begins the revelation of the church as the body of Christ from Romans 16 and Ephesians 3 and 5.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes on references: at about 1:28 the captions read “revelations 1 11” where he is describing “the revelation of Jesus Christ”; those words are Revelation 1:1 (which he cites again at about 4:34), so that passage is shown. At about 6:37 he gives “Revelation 22” (the last chapter) for “These words are faithful… the Lord God of the holy prophets sent His angel to show His servants”; those words are in Revelation 22:6, which is shown. At about 12:56 he says “Ecclesiastes” for “remember the Lord thy God in the days of thy youth before the evil day comes”; the passage in Ecclesiastes is 12:1 (“Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, before the difficult days come”), which is shown, and his wording differs. At about 22:59 the captions read “Romans 16:2 5”, which is Romans 16:25, and “Ephesians 33”, which is Ephesians 3:3. He names the other religious figures, preachers and denominations in this message himself; the claims about them are his own and have not been checked by this site. Where he reads Scripture aloud his wording often differs slightly from the NKJV text shown with each section.

chunks.section_question: Why does he say we should listen to John, who wrote Revelation on Patmos?
chunks.short_answer: He says John was banished to the isle of Patmos after being tarred and feathered for preaching the gospel, and that on the island, in that affliction, he received the book of Revelation. He says that when somebody pays a price like that, “we need to listen to them.”
chunks.text: This John got this on the isle of Patmos. He was banished by the local authorities to the isle of Patmos after he had been tarred and feathered and somehow survived for preaching the gospel. I mean, if you really want to go out and preach the gospel, people aren’t going to like you. It is not like the church in America today where we flatter people. And this is what you’re going to find in the book of Revelations, these guys that really went out and preached the gospel, they were [unclear], they were in prison, they were beaten, I mean they were subject to abuse all the time. Today, not so, because we’re really not preaching the gospel. We’re preaching a very flattering message that doesn’t challenge anyone, doesn’t shake up anyone. Most, now not all the church, but the majority of the church, and the majority of the church is on TV and radio, because you want numbers and you want money, you have to water down the message. You don’t want to hurt anybody’s feelings. But John wasn’t like that. He preached the gospel, he was tarred and feathered, and they banished him, and on that island, in that kind of affliction, he got this book of Revelation. chunks.section_question: What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?
chunks.short_answer: He says the book is the revelation of Jesus Christ, not of the beast or Satan, and that there are three revelations: of Jesus Christ, of the eternal judgment, and of the church. He says that if you read the Bible without looking for Jesus, “you’re going to miss the whole point of the Bible.”
chunks.text:
amen? Revelations 1:1, it starts out by saying “the revelation of Jesus Christ.” Not the beast, not the revelation of Satan, not the revelation of the [unclear] sitting on the seven mountains. Are you hearing me? It’s the revelation of who? Jesus Christ. This book is going to tell us about Jesus Christ. Revelation means to disclose, to reveal things, even things that have not been seen before. Okay, and so we’re going to have the revelation, the revealing, the disclosure of Jesus Christ. And we find that there’s three revelations in the New Testament. That’s the revelation of Jesus, the Lion, the Lamb, the Captain of the host, the Head of the church. I mean, He’s the big guy, He’s the chief honcho in the Bible, and when you read the Bible, if you’re not looking for Jesus, you’re going to miss the whole point of the Bible. Secondly, it’s the revelation of the

judgment. The Bible tells us there’s a revelation of the eternal judgment, and you don’t hear this message much anymore, that you’re going to be held accountable for what you say and do, and God is going to sentence you by what you say and do. You don’t hear this much anymore. When I was a kid you heard it all the time. They scared the hell out of you. I mean, man, you wanted Jesus and you wanted to get to heaven. But then we got into the love thing, everybody’s okay. And then the revelation of the church. I meet very few American Christians that even understand the basic revelation of the church. They think it’s a building with people in it. And I’d submit to you today, you don’t know it.

chunks.section_question: Is the church just a building with people in it?
chunks.short_answer: He says no: the Bible calls the church the body of Christ, each member with a particular function, and that it is also a flock, an army, and a house, a temple of God. He says that seeing what the church really is “should revolutionize” how you use your time and approach God.
chunks.text: Because if you did, it would change your life. It would change the way you do things. When we get through with the book of Revelation and you see what the church really is, it should revolutionize the way you schedule your time and you approach your God. It will make all the difference in the world, because the church isn’t some building with people in it. The Bible refers to it as the body of Christ. You see all those heads? See, we are the body of Christ and each one a member in particular, with a particular function. We have a function. Your little finger has a function. The smallest in God’s church has a function, a purpose and an objective. We are a flock, we follow the Shepherd, we need His protection, but we’re also an army, and we’re also a house, a temple of God. But we will get into that later, and this is what the Bible speaks of, these three revelations.

chunks.section_question: What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?
chunks.short_answer: He says Revelation 1:1 gives the revelation of Jesus Christ from God, things shown to “his servants,” which is all believers and not only the seven churches in Asia, and things that must shortly come to pass. He says we must pray for understanding of the scriptures because the Spirit is the only one who can open them to us.
chunks.text:
Now Revelations 1:1 has three points in it. Number one, the revelation of Jesus Christ, as we talked about, which God gave to Him. Who gave this to Him? God. All right. It’s not like Muhammad, it’s not like Joseph Smith. Those are imitators, as we’ll show you a little later. And you got to be [unclear]. You got to know

truth if you want to be free and you want others to be free. It’s the truth that sets you free. Free from what? Your traditions, your unbelief, your [unclear] doctrines, your doctrines of men. It sets you free from these things. Amen. And sin. Now number two, “to show unto His servants things.” Okay, He’s going to show us things, and it’s not just to the seven churches in Asia. To show unto His servants, all of us who accepted Christ. Christ is the King and we are His servants, and so He wants to show everybody, not just the seven churches of Asia. This is directed to everyone, isn’t that true? And He’s going to show us things. How many want your eyes open to the things He wants to show? Yeah. You got to pray. One of your main prayers is not only wisdom, but you need to pray that God gives you understanding of the scriptures, because the Spirit is the only one that can open the scriptures up to you. That’s what the Bible says, they are spiritually discerned. The Spirit has to do it. See, we can use our human intellect, but it is the Spirit that really bursts the truth in us.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about “shortly come to pass” and end-time prophecy teachers?
chunks.short_answer: He says the book plainly says these things must shortly come to pass, and that end-time prophets twist and stretch scriptures to make it fit our last days. He warns that what you believe determines your behavior, and says there are people making up their own doctrine today.
chunks.text: Amen. The things which must what? Shortly come to pass. He emphasizes it again. And what do all these end-time prophets do with Revelation? They twist and stretch all kinds of scriptures to get it to fit into our last days. Am I right? I am right. And it says plainly, these things must what? Shortly come to pass. Wow, you youngins got that? He says you need to take heed. Jesus told him, take heed, beware of the doctrine of the scribes and the Pharisees. Why? What you believe is what will determine your behavior. And the Pharisees had made up their own doctrine, and the Sadducees had made up their own doctrine, and have, you know, there’s people today making up their own doctrine, and people will try to please a church group in their doctrines of faith rather than please Christ and His book of faith. Could that be true? Now you young people understand this now. This is good stuff. This is deep stuff. This is not for the weak-hearted.

chunks.section_question: Did Judas believe in Jesus, and what does he say about believing and living right?

He says the gospel works no matter who preaches it, and that you get eternal life by believing, but if you believe on Jesus and live like Judas did, “you’re going to hell.”

faqs.question: Where did John get the book of Revelation?
faqs.answer: He says John got it on the isle of Patmos, where he was banished after being tarred and feathered for preaching the gospel.

faqs.question: What does “revelation” mean?
faqs.answer: He says it means to disclose or reveal, even things that have not been seen before, and this book is the revelation of Jesus Christ.

scriptures.text_nkjv: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John,

faqs.question: Who is the book of Revelation written to?
faqs.answer: He says it is not just for the seven churches in Asia but for all of God’s servants, everyone who has accepted Christ.

scriptures.text_nkjv: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John,

faqs.question: How do we get understanding of the scriptures?
faqs.answer: He says to pray, not only for wisdom but that God gives you understanding of the scriptures, because the Spirit is the only one who can open them to you.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him; nor can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.

faqs.question: What does he say sets us free?
faqs.answer: He says it is the truth that sets you free, from your traditions, your unbelief, your doctrines of men and sin.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.”

faqs.question: Is Revelation complicated?
faqs.answer: He says it isn’t complicated and isn’t 20 revelations, just three, and that you don’t need the Hebrew and Greek or someone on TV to tell you what it says.

faqs.question: Is judgment according to faith, grace or deeds?
faqs.answer: He reads that God renders to each one according to his deeds, and says that means your work, your lifestyle, how you speak and how you act.

scriptures.text_nkjv: who “will render to each one according to his deeds”:

faqs.question: Who gets eternal life, according to this message?
faqs.answer: He reads that eternal life goes to those who by patience and continuing in doing good patiently serve God, and says the first step is believing on Jesus.

scriptures.text_nkjv: eternal life to those who by patient continuance in doing good seek for glory, honor, and immortality;

faqs.question: Does the gospel work no matter who preaches it?
faqs.answer: He says someone preaching the gospel and the gospel working does not make the preacher great; it means the gospel is great, because the gospel works no matter who’s preaching it.

faqs.question: Who does he say faces wrath?
faqs.answer: He says there is wrath for those who are self-seeking, who do what they want, and for those who hear and don’t do it.

scriptures.text_nkjv: but to those who are self-seeking and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness—indignation and wrath,

faqs.question: What does he say about weapons of warfare?
faqs.answer: He says we have weapons of warfare that aren’t fleshly and we have to exercise them to tear down the strongholds of the enemy.

faqs.question: What good is believing in truth without obeying it?
faqs.answer: He says you can believe in truth, but if you don’t obey it, it does no good. He says the gospel doesn’t work for you if you don’t apply it.

faqs.question: Why is the Book of Life important?
faqs.answer: He says it should ignite us to praise God and thank Him, because through His death on the cross we can be forgiven and cleansed and our name written in His book.

faqs.question: What does 1 John 1:9 do for the record of our sins?
faqs.answer: He says that when you admit the sin and ask Christ to cleanse you, it is blotted out and your book has blank pages again. He adds that if we don’t repent, it stays in the book.

scriptures.text_nkjv: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

faqs.question: Is the church a denomination or association?
faqs.answer: He says the church is not a building or an association but His body, a many-membered body of Christ, chosen by God to be the messenger of His message.
